_mask_note: A filled block character stands where a word of the record's own title was removed.
_truncation: Values longer than 1200 characters are cut at 1200 and marked truncated:true. The full lengths are in data/sheet-truncation.json.

The North Sea Transition Authority's licensing system covers oil and gas within Great Britain, its territorial sea and on the UK Continental Shelf (UKCS).

The ▮ Act 1998 vests all rights to the nation's ▮ resources in the Crown, but the NSTA can grant licences that confer exclusive rights to 'search and bore for and get' ▮.

Licences fall into several categories. The principal distinctions are between ▮ and offshore licences, and between exploration licences (which cover exploration alone) and production licences (which cover both exploration and production).

The NSTA has discretion in the granting of licences to help maximise the economic recovery of the UK's oil and gas resources.

Licence data is represented by 3 different datasets;
